title: Week 7 Mastery Quiz · Executives, Legislatures, and Bureaucracies

questions.question: Fictional parliamentary record: a coalition loses a confidence vote under a rule requiring majority confidence. What should an analyst check next?
options: The head of government must immediately dissolve parliament regardless of constitutional procedures.
A confidence defeat always results in an automatic fresh election rather than another coalition.
The loss invalidates all legislation adopted before the vote.
Constitutional and procedural rules governing resignation, dissolution, or a new government
questions.explanation: Constitutional and procedural rules governing resignation, dissolution, or a new government

questions.question: An executive orders a regulation but the enabling statute limits the agency to issuing guidance. Which document comparison is necessary?
options: Executive directive, enabling statute, and relevant review decisions
questions.explanation: Executive directive, enabling statute, and relevant review decisions

questions.question: Simulated legislative data: 72 of 120 members support a bill, but the chamber requires two-thirds approval. What is the result?
options: The bill passes because 72 is a majority

questions.question: A legislature has broad oversight powers on paper, but ministers refuse to supply records. Which performance measure is most relevant?
options: Actual compliance with document requests and availability of remedies
Only the length of the constitution
questions.explanation: Actual compliance with document requests and availability of remedies

questions.question: Two cabinets have similar ministries, but one distributes appointments among coalition partners. Which records would test coalition bargaining?
options: Total size of the national territory
Coalition agreement, portfolio allocation, appointment records, and legislative voting
questions.explanation: Coalition agreement, portfolio allocation, appointment records, and legislative voting

questions.question: A public agency reports service completion rose from 70% to 90%, but its definition of completion changed midyear. What should a researcher do?
options: Treat the difference as proven performance gain
Attribute improvement to a single minister

questions.question: A president appoints ministers independently, while a prime minister depends on legislative confidence. What comparison avoids overgeneralizing?
options: Trace specific appointment, removal, and accountability rules in each constitution
One title always guarantees more authority
questions.explanation: Trace specific appointment, removal, and accountability rules in each constitution

questions.question: A fictional budget committee can request records but cannot sanction refusal. Which institutional dimension needs further examination?
options: Enforcement mechanisms and practical cooperation with oversight requests
questions.explanation: Enforcement mechanisms and practical cooperation with oversight requests

questions.question: A bureaucracy has detailed written procurement rules but repeated unexplained sole-source awards. What is the strongest evidence-oriented conclusion?
options: Examine procurement files, exceptions, and independent audit findings before judging compliance
questions.explanation: Examine procurement files, exceptions, and independent audit findings before judging compliance

questions.question: A policy fails in two districts despite identical national law. What follow-up helps distinguish implementation from statutory design?
options: Compare staffing, resources, local procedures, and measurable outcomes
Rewrite the national law as a slogan
questions.explanation: Compare staffing, resources, local procedures, and measurable outcomes

shortResponse: How do presidential, parliamentary, and hybrid systems organize leadership, representation, and administration?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
